hints: Look at what each part of the ion symbol tells you, the top number, bottom number and charge all mean something different.
Start by working out electrons for each ion, remember a negative charge adds electrons and a positive charge removes them.
Now compare neutrons using mass minus atomic number, then check if the proton numbers could ever match for two different elements.
walkthrough:
**Decode the symbols**

Remember the rules clearly. Bottom number is atomic number = protons. Top number is mass number = protons + neutrons. Charge tells you about electrons.

$$\text{neutrons} = \text{mass number} - \text{atomic number}$$

**Count particles in the phosphorus ion**

For $^{33}_{15}\text{P}^{3-}$, protons = 15. Neutrons = 33 - 15 = 18. Electrons = 15 + 3 = 18 because the 3- charge means 3 extra electrons.

**Count particles in the potassium ion**

For $^{37}_{19}\text{K}^{+}$, protons = 19. Neutrons = 37 - 19 = 18. Electrons = 19 - 1 = 18 because the + charge means 1 electron lost.

**Compare and decide**

Both ions have 18 electrons, so statement 1 is true. Both have 18 neutrons, so statement 2 is true. Protons are 15 vs 19, so statement 3 is false. That means 1 and 2 only are correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean statements 1, 2 and 3 are all true. Statements 1 and 2 are true, but statement 3 cannot be true because protons define the element, P has 15 and K has 19.
options.B: Correct. Both ions have 18 electrons and 18 neutrons, but different protons. So statements 1 and 2 only are true.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean statements 2 and 3 only are true. Statement 2 is true (both have 18 neutrons) but statement 3 is false and statement 1 is missed out.
options.D: Incorrect. This would mean statement 1 only is true. Statement 1 is true (both have 18 electrons) but statement 2 is also true and is missed out, both have 18 neutrons.
